1: Hello, my name is Marina, and I am a new student in this class. I am from Brazil, but I live in Canada now. I'm a computer technician at a small company. I am excited to practice English with other learners. My apartment is near the city library and a beautiful park. Are you from this city too?
2: Hello, I would like you to meet two of my friends. This is Pedro, and he is from Brazil. His sister is Sofia, and she is from Brazil too. They live in a small apartment near our school. Pedro works at a bakery, and Sofia studies history at the university. Nice to meet you both, and welcome to our English class!
3: Hello, this is Clara calling from the bus station near your office. Hi, Clara, this is Lucas, and I am waiting here in the reception area. Is the main entrance near the station or across the street? I'm sorry, but the main entrance is closed today. Please use the small entrance beside the coffee shop over there. Thank you, Lucas, I can see it now and will meet you inside.
4: I have a small notebook in my bag for new English words. I have a blue pen beside it and a pencil for drawings. I have an old phone with a photograph of my family. The phone isn't new, but it works very well. My bag also contains a bottle of water for the afternoon. These things help me study comfortably while I wait for the bus.
5: My home is small, but each room has a useful purpose. I cook dinner in the kitchen with my brother every evening. I read interesting stories in the living room after we eat. I brush my teeth in the bathroom before going to bed. I sleep in the bedroom beside the back garden. Where do you study when you need a quiet place in your home?
6: My apartment building is on a quiet street near the station. The gym is next to the lobby on the ground floor. A small store is across from the main entrance of our building. The garage is behind the building, beside a tall tree. Where is the mailroom in your apartment building? Our mailroom is near the elevator, so I check it on my way home.
7: I am studying English at the kitchen table while the house is busy. My sister is reading a book on the sofa near the window. My father is working on his computer in the next room. Our neighbors are talking quietly outside in their garden. What are you doing right now, and is your house as busy as mine?
8: In the morning, I eat breakfast and walk to the bus stop. In the afternoon, I work at a small office near the library. In the evening, I cook dinner and study English for twenty minutes. I follow this simple routine every day during the working week. My sister usually joins me for a short conversation after dinner. Right now, I am writing about my routine instead of watching television.
9: Is it cold outside today, or can we sit in the garden? Yes, it is cold, and the temperature is only eight degrees Celsius. Is it rainy too, or is the sky clear this morning? No, it is not rainy, but there are several clouds above the hills. We should wear warm coats if we walk to the park. That sounds sensible, and I will bring a scarf for you.
10: Exit the bus station through the doors beside the ticket office. Walk straight ahead past the bakery, then turn right at the traffic lights. Follow this street for two blocks, then turn left beside the library. My home is the small house with the blue gate. There is a quiet park directly opposite our front door. You can wait there if you arrive before I get home.
11: I need to complete several errands in my neighborhood this morning. First, I must buy two notebooks for my English class. I also need three envelopes and four stamps for some letters. Is there a post office near the station where I can buy them? Is there a bank on the same street as the bookshop? The bookshop is across from the library, so I can return my books too.
12: My mother works at a bakery and makes fresh bread every morning. My brother is a teacher who helps children learn to read. My aunt repairs bicycles in a small workshop near the park. What does your brother do when he finishes teaching for the day? What do your relatives enjoy doing together at weekends? In my family, we make lunch together and share stories about our different jobs.
13: On Sundays, I always eat breakfast slowly with my family at home. I usually visit my grandmother after we finish washing the dishes. I never work on Sundays, but today I am helping a colleague because she is ill. This is an unusual Sunday for me and for my family. My grandmother understands, and we plan to meet later this evening. Our usual walk can wait until I finish helping my colleague.
14: For an outdoor concert, I will wear a blue jacket over a white shirt. I will put on comfortable black shoes for the long walk. My red scarf will keep me warm during the cool evening. I can take off the heavy jacket inside the warm hall. How about a small gold necklace with the white shirt? The simple colors will match my favorite blue bag without looking too formal.
15: My friend Ana is tall, and her brother Leo is quite short. Ana has curly brown hair and dark eyes that look like her mother's. Leo has straight black hair and light brown skin. Both of them have friendly smiles and enjoy meeting new people. Today, they are waiting outside the station for our walking group. It is a beautiful day for a long walk together, isn't it?
16: My name is Rafael, and I am from Brazil, where my family still lives. I speak Portuguese at home and English with my classmates. My friend Luis is Mexican and speaks Spanish with his parents. Our teacher Helen is from Canada and understands a little Portuguese. We often compare interesting words from our different languages during lunch. What languages do you speak with your friends and family?
17: Next week, I am going to visit my grandmother on Monday afternoon. On Wednesday, I am going to attend an English class that I booked yesterday. The weather forecast looks cold, so I will take my warm coat. My brother has just asked for help, and I will help him after class. Are you free on Friday evening for a quiet dinner? We can choose a restaurant near the station if that is convenient.
18: First, the town library opened a new reading room for local children yesterday. Families often visit it after school, and volunteers help them choose books. Second, our neighborhood football team won an important match on Saturday afternoon. Its coach always thanks the players for working hard together. Third, a new bakery opened opposite the station this morning. The owner offered visitors small pieces of bread and invited us to come back.
19: I am choosing between a photography class and a cooking class near my home. The photography course begins next month and meets on Saturday mornings. The cooking course starts later, but its evening schedule is more convenient. Which one would help me enjoy my free time more? I already cook for my family every week and want to try something different. For that reason, I am leaning toward photography this time.
20: I could work in a small bookshop because I enjoy helping people find stories. I can organize books neatly on the shelves near the entrance. I can answer simple questions in English and explain where different sections are. I can also prepare attractive displays for special events at the shop. I can't manage the shop's accounts yet, and I can't repair its computer. Can you teach me how to use the sales system during my first week?
21: Would you like to come to our neighborhood festival on Saturday afternoon? First, I have to help my parents set up their small food stall. My brother has to bring the tables before the visitors arrive. Then we can listen to live music near the main entrance. We can also watch a short play performed by local students. I can't stay until midnight because I work early on Sunday. Please tell me when you can arrive so we can meet at the gate.
22: During our vacation, we are going to spend one whole day near the beach. First, we are going to walk along the shore before it gets crowded. Then we are going to have a picnic under the trees by the park. My sister wants to take photographs of the boats in the harbor. We can rest in a small cafe if the afternoon becomes too hot. Finally, we are going to watch the sunset before returning to our hotel.
23: What time does your cafe close this afternoon, before or after six? We close at six, but we are out of orange juice today. I want a sandwich and I want a bottle of water instead. The sandwich costs six dollars, and the water costs two dollars. That makes eight dollars altogether, so here is a ten-dollar note. Thank you, your change is two dollars, and your order will be ready soon.
24: Last Saturday, I visited a food festival in the park with my cousins. We walked past colorful stalls while a band played near the entrance. Later, we watched a group of children perform a traditional dance. My aunt cooked vegetable soup at a stall beside the stage. The weather was warm, so we stayed until the end of the afternoon. I saw a tool whose English name I do not know; you use it to squeeze fruit for fresh juice.
25: Watch out, because a bicycle is approaching the crossing beside you right now! Be careful, because the edge of the pavement is directly in front of your feet! You should stop walking before you read the map on your phone. You should also look in both directions before crossing this busy street. You ought to put the phone away until you reach a safe place to stand. The large clock reminds me of the town hall, and that association helps me remember this corner.
26: During a museum game, I found three symbols on a map near the entrance. I knew that the fish symbol represented the river beside the building. The mountain symbol reminds me of hiking with my family during our holidays. I associate the book symbol with the library because I often read there. My team won a small prize after we explained our answers to the guide. You ought to try this game with a friend because discussing the clues makes the visit more interesting.
27: Hello, I have a sore throat, a cough and a fever today. When did these symptoms start, and have they changed since yesterday evening? They started last night, and I felt very tired while preparing dinner. Did you sleep normally after you went to bed at your usual time? I slept badly, and I had some water when I woke up. You should rest at home while we arrange an assessment of these symptoms. Please drink fluids regularly and tell the clinician if your symptoms change. Thank you for explaining the next steps clearly and listening to my questions.
28: Yesterday, I took a practical test on using a camera in a busy room. The instructor was patient, but I was nervous about making a mistake. Start by checking the battery before you touch any other controls. Look at the screen to confirm that the picture is clear. Keep the camera steady with both hands while you record the scene. Stop recording when the person finishes speaking and moves out of view. I am sorry because I pressed the wrong button during my first attempt. Okay, I can slow down and try the instructions again one step at a time.
29: When I was a child, I lived in a small house near a quiet river. I played football with friendly neighbors after school almost every afternoon. I studied animals in an old notebook and read adventure stories at night. I wanted to become a wildlife photographer and travel around the world. I loved to take pictures of birds with my father's old camera. My favorite photograph showed a tiny bird resting on a wooden fence. Now I work in an office, but I still take my camera on weekend walks.
30: How much does a pound of these green apples cost today? A pound costs three dollars, and these are our freshest apples this morning. How many eggs are there in that box beside the apples? There are a dozen eggs in the box, and it costs four dollars. How much are the larger ears of corn near your sign? They are one dollar each and cheaper than the corn in the supermarket. How many ears would you like to take home for dinner? I would like three ears, a pound of apples and a dozen eggs, please. Your total is ten dollars, and you can pay with cash or credit. I will pay with cash, and here is the exact amount.
31: The metro is faster than the bus during the busy evening rush hour in my city. The bus is cheaper, but it often stops in heavy traffic near the center. I usually take the metro when I have an appointment downtown. Visitors should buy a transport card and check the station map before starting their journey.
32: A student asked why the moon sometimes looks larger near the horizon. I would first ask her what she had already read about the subject. Then I would find them an answer in a reliable science book with clear illustrations. I could show the whole class a diagram and explain the effect together. Whoa, I did not realize that our eyes could change the way we judge its size!
33: First, each player places four counters on the starting line of the board. Roll the die and move one counter forward by the number shown. Then the next player takes a turn and follows the same rule. If your counter lands on a star, move it forward one extra space. Finally, the first player to move all four counters to the finish wins the game.
34: I will attend my English class on Saturday morning because the booking is confirmed. After class, I might meet my cousin for lunch near the station. We might visit the museum if there are still tickets available. I have not bought a museum ticket because our afternoon plan is still uncertain. You won't forget to send me a message before you leave home, will you?
35: For dinner, I need a bag of rice and a bottle of olive oil. I also want a bunch of carrots to serve with the beans we already have. There are too many tomatoes in our kitchen, so I will make a small salad. My sister can buy the rice while I choose the vegetables. We should check the cupboard before leaving so that we do not buy anything twice.
36: The clean plates are inside the cupboard beside the kitchen window. The large frying pan is on the stove next to a small saucepan. You can find the wooden spoons in the drawer below the worktop. The washing-up bowl is under the sink, behind the cleaning cloths. I can see that the drawer is stuck, so I'll open it for you right now.
37: I agree that country life can be peaceful, especially when you enjoy spending time outdoors. However, I respectfully disagree that everyone would be happier far from a city. City life offers more transport choices than life in a small village. My sister prefers the countryside, and her favorite place is a quiet farm. Mine is a lively neighborhood where I can walk to work and meet friends easily.
38: Of all the people in my family, my aunt Rosa is the friendliest. She welcomes new neighbors and remembers the names of everyone she meets. She is also the most patient person I know when someone needs help. Last weekend, she spent an hour teaching my cousin to ride a bicycle. I admire her because she makes people feel comfortable without expecting anything in return.
39: I bought an inexpensive desk lamp online after reading an advertisement about its adjustable light. The advertisement said it would be useful for studying in a small room. It arrived on time, but the switch was loose and the box looked damaged. Fortunately, the light worked when I tested it carefully on my desk. I would not recommend this particular lamp because the build quality does not match the description.
40: Walk slowly across the room as if you are looking for a missing letter. Open the drawer carefully, then speak quietly when you discover the envelope inside. Your first performance was too fast for the audience to understand what you were searching for. Try opening the drawer later so that the suspense has time to build. In the final line, speak more loudly so that people at the back can hear you.
41: Good job on organizing the main ideas in your presentation for tomorrow's meeting. If you add one concrete example, your explanation will become easier to follow. If you practice the final paragraph aloud, you will feel more confident about the ending. You ought to check that the text on each slide is large enough to read. We can work together this afternoon and test the presentation before the meeting begins.
42: Yesterday, I was preparing dinner while my brother was finishing some work at the kitchen table. Suddenly, the lights went out, and we heard a loud noise outside. My brother found a torch while I checked that the cooker was safely switched off. I reminded myself to stay calm and avoid walking through the dark hallway. A few minutes later, our neighbor explained that a branch had fallen across a power line nearby. We waited together until the electricity returned and then finished our meal.
43: Could you help me carry these boxes to my new apartment this afternoon? I wish I could, but I have to finish an important report before five. That is all right, and thanks anyway for explaining your schedule to me. Would tomorrow morning be easier, when we both have more free time? Yes, I can meet you by the entrance at nine and bring a small trolley. That sounds like a good plan, and I will label the boxes tonight.
44: This week, I want to plan simple meals that my family enjoys eating together. We should buy a variety of vegetables instead of repeating the same dinner every evening. In our shared kitchen, everyone must label food that belongs to a particular person. We don't have to cook something complicated every night, especially when we are busy. A soup made from the vegetables already in the fridge can be an easy choice. I will write a shopping list so that we use what we have before buying more.
45: Next week, I will go to a coastal town for a short trip with my sister. At nine tomorrow morning, we will be traveling there on the train. At noon, we will be walking through the old harbor and looking at the boats. At six in the evening, we will be eating dinner near the beach. We also hope to visit the small museum if there is enough time before it closes. I will check the opening hours before we leave home.
46: May I borrow your camera for our class visit to the museum tomorrow? I can lend it to you if you keep it in its protective bag. Of course, and I will not let anyone else use it during the visit. Please avoid taking it outside if it begins to rain on the way home. I promise to return it on Friday morning before your photography lesson. Thank you for trusting me, and I will tell you immediately if anything goes wrong.
47: Why are you looking through those papers beside the computer right now? I am searching for the notes I need for our English presentation tomorrow. I was organizing them earlier, but I put one important page in the wrong folder. How can I help you find it before we leave for the evening? Please check the blue folder while I look through the papers on this table. I found the missing page myself, but thank you for offering to help me. Now we can finish preparing the presentation together without worrying about the notes.
48: I have visited several interesting places in my city since moving here last year. The central market is my favorite because people sell food from many different regions. I have never seen the inside of the old theater, although I walk past it every week. Visitors should leave enough time to explore the market's smaller stalls and talk to the sellers. You can take a bus from the station and get off beside the main entrance. I recommend going early in the morning before the streets become crowded.
49: I have completed the first part of my mission and delivered the sealed envelope safely. Yesterday at noon, I met my contact outside the museum's side entrance. She gave me a map and explained where the next meeting would take place. I am now waiting in a cafe where I can watch the station doors. My partner is checking the meeting location before we move to the next stage. Nobody has approached us, and the envelope was never left unattended during the journey. I will send another report as soon as our contact arrives.
50: I have been studying English for six months because I want to speak more confidently at work. My friend has been practicing with me since the beginning of our evening course. We listen to a short conversation and then explain its main ideas to each other. Every Friday, I review the new expressions in my notebook and check an older recording. I notice that I pause less often when I describe familiar activities now. Comparing recordings helps me see progress without expecting every sentence to be perfect.
51: My goal is to hold a short conversation in English without preparing every sentence first. I enjoy listening to stories about everyday life because their situations are easy to imagine. I have been practicing for fifteen minutes each evening since the start of this month. After listening, I describe the story aloud and record a few sentences on my phone. I want to ask clearer questions when I meet visitors at work. My daily habit supports that goal by giving me regular opportunities to speak. I also plan to ask a classmate for feedback once a week.
52: I have learned to introduce myself, describe my routine and ask for help during my English course. When I started last year, I found it difficult to understand short questions spoken at normal speed. I listened again, wrote down useful phrases and practiced them with a patient classmate. The phrasal verb look up became useful because I often needed to look up unfamiliar words. I can now understand the main idea of many familiar conversations without reading every line first. I still need practice explaining my opinions clearly and connecting longer ideas. Next month, I will begin the second level and continue recording a short reflection after each lesson.
